prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope:offshore-wind acceptance/O&M/refurbishment/decommissioning;external-grid/unrelated-ports excluded;reporting active;software integrity/availability controlled. Aliases/flows:Glassfin=Turbine Controller→Pitch Deviation Notice;Morrowick=Offshore Substation→Transformer Tap Snapshot→Amber Quay=Shore Control Room→Switching Window Acknowledgment→Offshore Substation(confirms approved-window availability);Pale Lantern=Weather Service→Squall Window Bulletin→Thistle Crown=Maintenance Planning Engine→Deferred Task Rationale(weather/reprioritization/cyber,not-safety);Juniper Vale=SCADA Gateway→Session Revocation Receipt→Quiet Harbor=Cybersecurity Gateway;SCADA alarms/status/observations→Amber Quay(source timestamps preserved where available);Kestrel Bay=Crew Transfer Vessel;Sable Orchard=Fleet Dispatch Console;Mosslight=Warehouse System→Backorder Exception Slip→Storekeeper;Copper Finch=Metocean Buoy→Wave Burst Record→Pale Lantern/Weather Analyst;Blue Granite=Vessel AIS Receiver→Position Quality Flag→Sable Orchard,positions→Marine Coordinator;Larkspur=Blade Inspection Drone→Leading Edge Tile Image;Redoubt=Work Permit Portal→Isolation Boundary Sketch→Electrical Technician/work-party/control-team;Foxglove=Emergency Generator→Start Test Trace;Wildmere=Grid Interface Relay. Elements:Pitch System;Converter Cabinet;Nacelle Condition Monitor;Rotor Brake Unit;Turbine Sensor Bus;Main Transformer;Export Cable Monitor;Spares Hub;Daughter Craft;Helideck;Service Operations Vessel→Recovery Basket Load Sheet→Rescue Coordinator(security/accounting);North Access Scanner/South Access Scanner→personnel-access-events;Personnel Tracking Console→counts/corrections/verified-total/safe-return-confirmation. Requirements:Control Engineer verifies compatibility/purpose/scope/sequence/changes/recovery/restart/indications;remote-shutdown requires safe-communications/status;release authorized/gradual/monitored. Substation Operator verifies status/authority/test-trace/limits/range;switching-operator reports;ambiguity/communications-failure/deviation→pause/safe-state. Duty Planner checks personnel/permits/recovery-conflicts;logs approvals/sequence/roles/communications/final-state/deviations/restrictions/handover/actual-times;prioritizes shortages. Grid Dispatcher←Export Limit Advisory;sets permitted-level/confirms restrictions. Isolation:site-approved.

New part:
S768: The Control Engineer reviews alarms and operating trends with the SCADA Engineer when an abnormal condition may require intervention.
S769: The Grid Dispatcher communicates external operating requirements to the Grid Interface Relay and the responsible control personnel.
S770: Instructions that affect electrical safety are communicated through authorized channels and confirmed by the responsible Substation Operator or Electrical Technician.
S771: When a communication channel is unavailable, personnel use the approved fallback method and report the outage as soon as practicable.
S772: Urgent messages identify the affected asset, the hazard or condition, the required action, and the person issuing the instruction.
S773: The receiver repeats critical details, and the sender confirms that the read-back is accurate before the instruction is treated as understood.
S774: Operational records identify the originator, recipient, event time, recording time, relevant asset, and decision or action taken.
S775: Entries distinguish observed facts from estimates, assumptions, and recommendations so that later reviewers can assess their basis.
S776: Records use synchronized time sources where available, and any known clock discrepancy is noted for later reconciliation.
S777: Corrections preserve the original entry, identify the person making the change, and state the reason for the correction.
S778: The Field Supervisor ensures that field observations and work outcomes are entered promptly while the details remain verifiable.
S779: The Duty Planner links relevant communications and work records to the applicable work package and operating plan.
S780: The Work Permit Portal retains permit decisions and associated approvals in a form that can be retrieved for review.
S781: The Cybersecurity Analyst protects access logs and communication records against unauthorized alteration or disclosure.
S782: The organization retains voice recordings, system logs, and work records according to the approved retention schedule and applicable legal obligations.
S783: Records subject to an investigation, claim, or safety review are preserved from routine deletion until the authorized release of the hold.
S784: The responsible manager reviews record completeness after significant events and assigns correction or follow-up actions where evidence is missing.
S785: Fire protection is designed to detect smoke, heat, and flame early enough to support automatic equipment protection and a controlled personnel response.
S786: The Fire Detection Panel supervises detection circuits and annunciates alarms with location and fault information.
S787: Detection coverage includes electrical enclosures, machinery spaces, and other areas identified by the site fire risk assessment.
S788: The Turbine Sensor Bus carries equipment status used by protective functions and operational monitoring.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
